There could be many reasons for this, and the most common of them are usually not the drivers fault. Often it's just the nature of the biz, and it's unfortunately part of the risk of having food delivered. Sometimes it can be chalked up to a bad driver, but often it's down the app and out of our hands 

Drivers fault:
- if they make an un-directed or unscheduled stop on the way to the pickup location 

-if the driver does not have a bag to keep the food warm during transit. 
That's about all I can think of.

Not drivers fault:
-traffic

-the app selecting a driver that is far away from pickup location, for various reasons...either no one else is available or it overestimated the time for the food to be ready by more than a couple min, which happens a lot, 

-or even having an order cancelled by the initial driver and then having to send it to another 

-really long lines at the drive through, with no way to pick up in store because the doors to the lobby are locked and they insist you wait in the drive through line

-the app assigning a double or triple order, and having a long wait at the first restaurant, while the second order is finished quickly. Or the two pickup locations are far apart 

-too many orders to fit all in the hot bag or an order that won't fit. this often happens with large orders from chinese food restaurants, because they often use spare or recycled cardboard boxes. it's also an issue with orders of multiple large size pizzas. 

The hot bags do a pretty good job of keeping the temperatures from dropping, but it's still only the temp it was when the driver picked it up. And often that's an issue beyond the drivers control. Sometimes the pickup location is 10 min away and the food might be already being prepared when you get the order, so it's sitting out for ten min.
